sourceDesign.exportCommand: Pencil MCP execute on a byte-identical scratch copy (/tmp): Export(["vARtQ"], "png", "<repo>/e2e/references/paf-10", {scale:2})
sourceDesign.provenanceNote: T10 (PAF-10) reference for the Player profile frame vARtQ, exported uncropped at 2x through Pencil MCP from a scratch copy whose SHA-256 equals the tracked source (and the paf-6/7/8 manifests). The tracked .pen was not modified. The frame is a mockup with stats tiles, a month-based dot chart and a bottom navigation that the production dashboard does not render; the T10 rating journey instead uses a game-ordered chart, a data table and a drill-down explanation dialog, which have no dedicated frame.

vARtQ.certifies: Profile top region (title, identity hero, global level card) and the Rating journey section order

visualBudgets.measurementMethod: Clip the production capture to the 390x308 CSS-px top region (deviceScaleFactor 1) and compare with the same region of the 2x Pencil PNG downsampled by 2, using the pinned perceptual threshold (35215 x 0.1^2). Structural probes (order, gutters, containment, 44px targets, no overflow) assert geometry separately and exactly.

perScreenRationale.vARtQ: Observed residual 0.0862 on the title-aligned 390x308 top region; 0.10 leaves 0.0138 for cross-renderer variance. The residual is intentional route/data adaptation, not a layout defect: the frame's blank avatar circle, 'Right side · Madrid' and 'Member since 2024' versus production initials, real side and localized join date; the '76% reliable' pill versus 'Reliability: N%'; and live level values. Order, gutters, chart containment, row stacking, 44px targets and overflow are exact structural probes. The stats tiles, month-dot chart and bottom navigation of the frame are out of scope (no standings/stats product); the game-ordered chart, data table and explanation dialog have no frame and are covered by structural/contrast probes plus attached screenshots.
